=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly radiating from a single node)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are densely arranged at the apex of the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are undivided)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (margins appear smooth, though some leaves have irregular holes/damage)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic to obovate (broadest point is distal to the middle)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (wedge-shaped, tapering gradually to the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (one main midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): highly visible, prominent, and regularly spaced
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny and rugose (appears glossy and has a textured surface due to prominent veins)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth and glabrous)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are very brief, appearing almost sessile)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (cylindrical, not winged or grooved)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears rigid and lignified)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: reddish-brown (visible at the central node and petiole bases)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): unclear (cannot definitively confirm presence or absence due to the clustered arrangement and angle)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a distinctive rosette-like growth habit with leaves whorled at the apex. The venation is strongly impressed, giving the leaf surface a corrugated appearance. Several leaves show signs of damage in the form of holes and missing tissue.
